newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: SOCCER-ETHIOPIA TOP LIST OF CUP UPSETS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ETHIOPIA TOP LIST OF CUP UPSETS.

text.p: Ethiopia put last month's defection of almost all their team behind them to hold Egypt to a draw in their African Nations' Cup qualifying match on Sunday.
The result was one of several upsets in the weekend's qualifiers which saw teams take points off more fancied opposition.
Benin held Algeria to a 1-1 tie at home while Mauritius won their first Nations Cup point in almost four years with a goalless draw against Zambia.

An injury time goal kept alive tiny Togo's hopes of qualifying for the finals in Burkina Faso next February and Tanzania held a Liberian team, spearheaded by George Weah, for their first spoils of the campaign.
But Ethiopia's point was the most improbable of the lot, coming just a month after 16 players defected in Rome on route to a match in Morocco.

Ethiopia were forced to put together a new team for the group four match against Egypt in Addis Ababa and were not given any chance against one of the continent's strongest sides who had put seven goals past Ethiopia in their last two encounters.
But the home team shocked the visitors by taking the lead through Aseyed Tesfaye 13 minutes into the second-half before Egypt scored a face-saving equaliser 19 minutes from time.

Benin were also ahead in their group two game against Algeria, Nations Cup winners seven years ago, courtesy of a first-half goal from Moussa Latounji before Abdelhafid Tasfaout, who plays for Auxerre in France, equalised shortly after half-time.
Kossi Noutsoudje kept up Togo's unbeaten run with an injury-time equaliser against Zaire in Lome in group six.
Zaire had opened the scoring through Belgian-based midfielder Ekanza Simba. The result leaves the two teams comfortably ahead of group favourites Liberia, who drew 1-1 in Tanzania on Saturday.

AC Milan striker George Weah returned to the Liberian team after missing their last two matches but it was his Swiss-based colleague Jonathan Sogbie who scored to put the Lone Stars ahead before the home side equalised in the last 15 minutes.
Mauritius' home draw with Zambia in group seven on Sunday was another upset and provided the Indian Ocean islanders with a rare point.

Ivory Coast gained a hard-fought 2-1 away win over neighbours Mali with veteran Joel Tiehi scoring the winner while the weekend's other victors included Zimbabwe, with a controversial 1-0 win over Angola on Sunday, and Malawi, whose 2-0 win over Mozambique on Saturday breathed new life into their qualifying campaign.
